items.title: fix(oauth-provider): leave request bodies alone when the page query is unsigned

labels.name: identity
labels.description: OAuth/OIDC provider, device flow

items.body: Closes #12072 The `oauth-provider-signin` hook re-serialized every POST body whenever the page had any query string. With no `sig`/`ba_param`, `buildSignedOAuthQuery` returns undefined, but the body had already gone through `safeJSONParse` and `JSON.stringify`, so ISO date strings came back as `Date` output and form bodies were sent as JSON under a form content type. Now the hook returns early when there is no signed query. On a signed page, form bodies stay form encoded with `oauth_query` appended, and JSON bodies are parsed with plain `JSON.parse` so date strings are not rewritten. Tests cover unsigned pages (JSON and form bodies sent byte-identical) and signed pages (form encoding kept, dates unchanged, `oauth_query` added). --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #12072 by stopping `oauthProviderClient` from rewriting request bodies when the page query isn't a signed OAuth query. Previously, any query string caused the hook to parse and re-serialize the body even when `buildSignedOAuthQuery` returned undefined, converting ISO date strings to `Date` output and sending form bodies as JSON under a form content type. The hook now returns early when there is no signed query. On signed pages, bodies also keep their original encoding: form bodies stay form-encoded and date strings are left as written while `oauth_query` is added, and JSON parse failures are logged. Tests cover byte-identical JSON and form bodies on unsigned pages and `oauth_query` still being added on signed pages. Written for commit 707b2eda905d195f66f7c61b535f465b9c214ded. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: feat(oauth-popup): accept additionalParams like signIn.social
items.body: ## Summary Closes #12119 `signIn.social` accepts `additionalParams`, but `signIn.popup` had no equivalent, so request-dependent parameters such as `ui_locales` could not be passed to the provider. This adds the option to `signIn.popup`, with the same validation as `/sign-in/social`. ## Changes - `signIn.popup` accepts `additionalParams?: Record` and sends it to `/oauth-popup/start` as a JSON query param (same transport as `additionalData`). - `/oauth-popup/start` validates it with `additionalAuthorizationParamsSchema` (string values only; reserved keys such as `state`, `redirect_uri` and PKCE params are rejected) and passes the result to `createAuthorizationURL`. - Invalid params are relayed to the opener as an `invalid_additional_params` completion error, consistent with the other start-stage failures, so the opener does not wait for a timeout. - Changeset added (`minor`). ## Security consideration `/oauth-popup/start` is a GET endpoint, so `originCheckMiddleware` does not apply, unlike the POST `/sign-in/social`. This means a link to the start endpoint can now influence provider-specific authorization parameters (e.g. `login_hint`, `prompt`, `hd`). The impact looks limited: the completion message is only posted to a trusted `popupOrigin`, and a start link could already be used to begin a flow without params. I followed the approach proposed in the issue (plain pass-through with the shared schema). If maintainers prefer something stricter, such as an allowlist option on `oauthPopup()`, I'm happy to rework it. ## Testing - Server: params are forwarded to the provider authorization URL; a reserved key (`state`) is rejected; a non-string value is rejected. - Client: params are serialized into the start URL and omitted when unset. - `pnpm vitest run src/plugins/oauth-popup` passes (20 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` passes. There are no docs for `signIn.popup` under `docs/content`, so none were updated; the option is documented via JSDoc. --- ## Summary by cubic `signIn.popup` now accepts `additionalParams` so request-dependent provider parameters like `ui_locales` can be passed, matching `signIn.social` (closes #12119). - The popup client serializes `additionalParams` into the `/oauth-popup/start` URL as a JSON query param, omitted when unset. - The server validates it with `additionalAuthorizationParamsSchema` (string values only; reserved keys like `state` and `redirect_uri` rejected) and forwards the result to `createAuthorizationURL`; invalid params return an `invalid_additional_params` completion error instead of leaving the opener waiting for a timeout. ISO-8601 values stay strings rather than being coerced to dates. **Security consideration** - `/oauth-popup/start` is a GET endpoint, so `originCheckMiddleware` does not apply; a start link can now influence provider params like `login_hint` or `prompt`, but the completion message is still only posted to a trusted `popupOrigin`. **Testing** - Server tests cover forwarding, reserved-key rejection, non-string rejection, and ISO-8601 string preservation; client tests cover serialization and omission when unset. Written for commit 232cfe6b6838cbfbe9aadb79d09a17e154dbda83. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(oauth-provider): persist and enforce client secret expiry

labels.name: identity
labels.description: OAuth/OIDC provider, device flow

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Documentation, demos

items.body: ## Summary `client_secret_expires_at` never reached the database. The `oauthClient` schema has had no column for it since the plugin landed, although `SchemaClient` and both mappers expect `expiresAt`. Managed registration also replaced the admin's value with `0`. Every response reported `0`, and a secret past its expiry kept authenticating, contrary to the "Create Client" and "Dynamic Client Registration Expiration" docs and [RFC 7591 §3.2.1](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc7591#section-3.2.1). ```diff persistOAuthClientRegistration dynamic → clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration ?? 0 - managed → 0 + managed → admin's client_secret_expires_at ?? 0 - adapter.create # expiresAt dropped, no column + adapter.create # new optional oauthClient.expiresAt validateClientCredentials # token, introspect, revoke verify secret + expiresAt <= now → invalid_client "client secret has expired" ``` - Expiry is checked only after the secret matches, so a caller without the secret learns nothing about it, and `private_key_jwt` clients are never affected. - A string value is a time span from now (`"90d"`), as in `clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration`. Any other string returns 400 `invalid_client_metadata`. - `adminUpdateOAuthClient` with `0` clears the expiry. Rotation keeps it, so a client owner cannot outlast an admin-set expiry. ## Evidence New `client-secret-expiry.test.ts`, through `auth.api` and `auth.handler`: ```text registerOAuthClient with clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration: "30d" main: client_secret_expires_at 0, no stored expiresAt now: issued_at + 30d in the response, the row, and getOAuthClient adminCreateOAuthClient { client_secret_expires_at: now - 3600 }, then client_credentials main: response reports 0 now: 401 invalid_client ``` - **Before:** 5 of 6 fail on `main`. **After:** 6 of 6 pass. Reverting only the `validateClientCredentials` check turns both `invalid_client` tests red. The oauth-provider suite (1026 tests) and `pnpm typecheck` pass. ## Merge Danger **Door:** one-way The `expiresAt` column lands in users' databases, so renaming or removing it later takes another migration. **Blast Radius:** migration - `minor` changeset, so release automation moves this to `next`. - The column must exist before deploy. Prisma and Drizzle read every declared column, so deploying a regenerated client or schema before migrating breaks every OAuth client read, with or without an expiry. Until the column exists, writes that carry an expiry also fail: admin create or update with `client_secret_expires_at`, and every dynamic registration that issues a client secret when `clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration` is set. This is read from the adapter code; only SQLite ran. - Clients registered before the upgrade have no stored expiry and still never expire. --- ## Summary by cubic Persists and enforces OAuth client secret expiry. Previously the value was dropped, every response reported `client_secret_expires_at: 0`, and a secret past its expiry kept authenticating. The expiry now saves to a new optional `oauthClient.expiresAt` column, reports in registration and read responses, and makes the token, introspection, and revocation endpoints reject an expired secret with `invalid_client` (only after the secret matches). Managed registration keeps the admin-set expiry, `adminUpdateOAuthClient` clears it with `0`, rotation preserves it, and string values like `"90d"` are read as time spans from now; empty strings, non-time-span strings, and out-of-range values are rejected with `invalid_client_metadata`. **Related fixes** - DPoP proofs validate against the concrete request path, resolving route params (e.g. `/extension/acme/token`) and keeping trailing slashes when `advanced.skipTrailingSlashes` is on. - New `allowClientKeyRotation` option lets `private_key_jwt` clients with inline `jwks` replace their own signing keys via `POST /oauth2/client/rotate-keys`. Off by default; refuses to start on the memory adapter or with `generateId: "serial"`. - Updates, deletes, and secret rotations of clients listed in `cachedTrustedClients` now return `invalid_client` with HTTP 400 instead of 500. - Adds black-box DPoP interop smoke tests using `oauth4webapi` and forces both orderings of the revoke-vs-rotate refresh race in tests. **Migration** This adds a nullable column to the `oauthClient` table. Run `npx auth@latest migrate` with the built-in Kysely adapter, or `npx auth@latest generate` and apply the change with Prisma or Drizzle, migrating before deploying the regenerated client or schema; MongoDB needs nothing. Until the column exists, writes carrying an expiry fail and dynamic registration fails when `clientRegistrationClientSecretExpiration` is set. Clients registered before the upgrade have no stored expiry and still never expire. Written for commit 56e3c0441b0c4120f55b1dcfc46a29ecf65909d7. Summary will update on new commits.

items.body: ## What Adds opt-in \ efreshToken(refreshToken, ctx?)\ provider-config override to the \genericOAuth\ plugin. When present, the override runs instead of the default form-encoded \ okenUrl\ POST. \^GccessTokenExpiresIn\ still applies as expiry fallback on the custom path. \ efreshTokenParams\ and \ okenEndpointAuth\ do not apply on the custom path. ## Why Providers whose token exchange goes through \getToken\ (JSON body, custom auth, or no \ okenUrl\) previously had no refresh path without a standard token endpoint. This unblocks refresh for JSON-only \getToken\ providers while keeping the form default untouched. ## Linked Fixes #11559 (partial, A2). Part of #11607. Respects #11370. ## Breaking NONE — additive optional field, default behavior unchanged. ## Testing - vitest refreshToken suite: 3 passed - full generic-oauth suite: 134 passed - typecheck clean ## Risk Low (additive opt-in). Docs warn: custom \ etch\ in the hook runs outside \ etchRefusingRedirects\ (redirects are not refused) and without \BLOCKED_REFRESH_TOKEN_PARAMS\ filtering — pin the URL, refuse redirects, never log secrets (SSRF/blocklist warning in docs). ## Rollback git revert ## Reviewer notes - Hook-first branch: override checked before any \ okenUrl\ requirement, so \getToken\-only providers can refresh. - Guard shape: override must return a tokens object; anything else throws fail-closed \OAuthGenericRefreshFailed\. - Opaque-redirect example in docs shows pinning URL + refusing redirects + no secret logging. ## API delta Added optional \ efreshToken?: (refreshToken: string, ctx?: GenericOAuthContext) => Promise | OAuth2Tokens | null | undefined\ to genericOAuth provider config. --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an opt-in `refreshToken` override to the `genericOAuth` provider config so providers whose token exchange goes through a custom `getToken` (JSON body, custom auth, or no `tokenUrl`) can refresh without a standard form-encoded token endpoint. Partially addresses #11559. The hook runs instead of the default `tokenUrl` POST, `accessTokenExpiresIn` still applies as an expiry fallback, and the override type requires a string `accessToken` — anything else fails closed with `INVALID_OAUTH_CONFIGURATION`. The hook receives a sanitized `ctx` limited to `{ headers, request }`. The docs example uses a nullish expiry check so an `expires_in` of `0` is preserved instead of falling back. **Notes** - `refreshTokenParams` and `tokenEndpointAuth` do not apply on the custom path; the hook owns the whole request. - Custom `fetch` in the hook runs outside `fetchRefusingRedirects` and without `BLOCKED_REFRESH_TOKEN_PARAMS` filtering — docs instruct pinning the URL, refusing redirects, and never logging secrets. - No breaking changes: the field is additive and form-based refresh behavior is unchanged when the override is absent. Written for commit 072be9659b84117f25b59ce5e6fe76d29c505c7b. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: CLI drizzle generator emits bare timestamp(...) for Postgres; should support timestamptz

labels.name: breaking
labels.description: Would break existing behavior

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

labels.name: devtools
labels.description: CLI, OpenAPI, telemetry, i18n, test-utils

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
## What

`packages/cli/src/generators/drizzle.ts` hardcodes the PG date column as:

\`\`\`ts
date: {
  sqlite: \`integer('\${name}', { mode: 'timestamp_ms' })\`,
  pg: \`timestamp('\${name}')\`,
  mysql: \`timestamp('\${name}', { fsp: 3 })\`,
},
\`\`\`

The PG branch produces `timestamp('${name}')`, which Drizzle maps to Postgres `timestamp without time zone`.

## Why this is wrong for these columns

Every date column emitted by the generator — `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `expiresAt`, `lastUsedAt`, `accessTokenExpiresAt`, `refreshTokenExpiresAt` — represents an absolute-time event. `timestamp without time zone` is a wall-clock string type: it has no UTC offset, and Postgres reinterprets it at the connection's `TimeZone` setting on read. A session token stored as `expiresAt` from a process in `UTC` will be read back as a wall-clock string and re-interpreted as the reader's session timezone, silently producing a different absolute moment.

`timestamptz` (Drizzle: `timestamp(name, { withTimezone: true })`) is the correct mapping. Postgres internally stores the UTC instant and returns it correctly regardless of session timezone.

## What I expected

The generator emits `timestamp('${name}', { withTimezone: true })` for PG by default, or accepts an option for it.

## Workaround in the meantime

Hand-patch `auth-schema.ts` after every regen to add `{ withTimezone: true }`. Vulnerable to silent drift on the next regen.

## Proposed change

Either:
1. Switch the default PG mapping to `timestamp('${name}', { withTimezone: true })`. Existing users who care about wall-clock semantics for some reason can override per-column.
2. Add a CLI flag / config option (e.g. `dateMode: 'utc' | 'local'`) and default to `'utc'`.

Option 1 is the right default for an auth library: every column in the generated schema represents an absolute moment.

## Repro context

- better-auth `1.4.20`
- `@better-auth/cli generate` against Postgres + Drizzle adapter
- Generated columns observed with `pg_typeof(created_at)` returning `timestamp without time zone`

## Related community workaround

Examples of users patching the generated file by hand after regen, e.g. [this Nuxt + better-auth + drizzle guide](https://www.madebyfabian.com/blog/how-to-setup-better-auth-with-nuxt-3-and-drizzle).

labels.description: SSO (OIDC + SAML), SCIM provisioning

items.body: Add an opt-in `userSchemaExtensions` option to the SCIM plugin. Declared extensions are advertised through /Schemas and the User ResourceType, validated on ingress, stored, round-tripped in responses, and support schema-qualified PATCH (add/replace/remove). Each attribute may optionally be mapped to a `user.additionalFields` key so it is queryable outside SCIM. Only simple singular attributes are supported (string, boolean, integer, decimal, dateTime, reference); complex and multi-valued attributes are out of scope. Custom extensions are lenient about schema declaration — a present extension value auto-declares its URN — for interoperability with providers such as Microsoft Entra, while the Enterprise extension keeps its strict contract. Startup validation checks that each mapped field exists, is optional, and is type-compatible, and warns when a mapped field is end-user writable. The static User schema graph is refactored into builder factories fed per instance, keeping the existing constants as zero-extension defaults so behavior is unchanged when no extensions are declared. Closes #10980 --- ## Summary by cubic Adds an opt-in `userSchemaExtensions` option to the SCIM plugin so applications can carry custom User attributes through provisioning. Declared extensions are advertised through `/Schemas` and the User ResourceType, validated on ingress, stored, round-tripped in responses, and support schema-qualified PATCH; each attribute can optionally map to a `user.additionalFields` key to be queryable outside SCIM. **Scope** - Only simple singular attributes are supported (string, boolean, integer, decimal, dateTime, reference); `dateTime` values must be real RFC 3339 dates and map to a `Date` on the user field. Complex and multi-valued attributes are out of scope. - Custom extensions auto-declare their URN when an extension value is present, so providers such as Microsoft Entra can omit the declaration; the Enterprise extension keeps its strict contract. - Startup validates that each mapped field exists, is optional, and is type-compatible, and warns when a mapped field is end-user writable. Case-variant attribute names are canonicalized on ingress, and `returned: "never"` attributes are stripped from responses. - PATCH matches the longest URN prefix and validates root fragments per attribute; a pathless op merges and a `null` value clears only the targeted attribute, while `replace` on the extension root replaces and clears omitted attributes. - Per-attribute selection via `attributes`/`excludedAttributes` is not yet supported for custom extension attributes; full-resource GET still returns them. **Refactors** - The static User schema graph is now built per instance via builder factories; existing constants remain zero-extension defaults, so behavior is unchanged when no extensions are declared. Closes #10980 Written for commit cf3a4c2410109a502d27751cd868001b787f648b. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(db): never write the active-sessions list with a zero ttl

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

items.body:
## Summary

Three secondary-storage writes gated the `active-sessions` list on a millisecond expiry while passing a ttl in whole seconds. A list whose furthest remaining session is under a second from expiry passes the gate but floors to a ttl of `0`, and secondary storage reads a zero ttl as "no expiry", so the key is stored permanently.

Closes #10992

## The inconsistency

`getTTLSeconds` floors to whole seconds and clamps at zero, so these three gates are checking the wrong unit:

- `deleteCachedUserSessions`: `if (furthestExpiration)` (truthy only)
- `updateSession`: `if (furthestSessionExp && furthestSessionExp > now)`
- `deleteSession`: `if (filtered.length > 0 && furthestSessionExp && furthestSessionExp > Date.now())`

The session write in the same file already does it correctly:

```ts
const furthestSessionTTL = getTTLSeconds(furthestSessionExp, now);
if (furthestSessionTTL > 0) { ... }
```

## The fix

Each site now computes the ttl once and gates on it, so a zero never reaches `set()` and the existing `else` branch deletes the key instead.

```diff
-		if (furthestExpiration) {
+		const listTTL = furthestExpiration
+			? getTTLSeconds(furthestExpiration, now)
+			: 0;
+		if (listTTL > 0) {
 			await secondaryStorage.set(
 				activeSessionsKey,
 				JSON.stringify(remainingSessionReferences),
-				getTTLSeconds(furthestExpiration, now),
+				listTTL,
 			);
```

No new helper: this reuses the pattern already present in the file.

## Tests

One test on the `deleteSession` path, which is the most commonly reached of the three: seed the list with one entry 300ms out and one an hour out, delete the hour-out token, and assert the rewritten list carries a positive ttl.

It fails on the unpatched code with `expected 0 to be greater than 0`, which is the bug.

`internal-adapter.test.ts` is 68/68 and `pnpm typecheck` reports no new errors. The one failing test in `db.test.ts` (`preserve a forced UUID on postgres`) needs Docker and fails identically on a clean `main`.

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

labels.name: docs

labels.description: Locked conversations after being closed for 7 days

labels.name: devops
labels.description: CI/CD, GitHub Actions, build tooling, e2e tests, release automation

items.body: ## Summary A Drizzle schema that stores dates in string columns broke every Better Auth write. Drizzle passes the value of `timestamp({ mode: "string" })`, MySQL `datetime({ mode: "string" })` and SQLite `text()` to the driver unchanged, and in Drizzle 0.45 those columns have no driver mapping, so the adapter's `Date` reached the driver: | Driver | On `main` | |---|---| | postgres-js | `TypeError: The "string" argument must be of type string ... Received an instance of Date` | | better-sqlite3 | `SQLite3 can only bind numbers, strings, bigints, buffers, and null` | | Cloudflare D1 | `D1_TYPE_ERROR: Type 'object' not supported` (#10816) | Email sign-up returned 422 `FAILED_TO_CREATE_USER`, and filters on those columns, such as `expiresAt > now` when listing sessions, failed the same way. The Drizzle 1.0 relations adapter has the same problem for SQLite `text()`. A second bug sat behind the first. A string without a time zone, as PostgreSQL `timestamp` and MySQL `datetime` return, was read with `new Date(value)`, which parses it as the server's local time. On a server outside UTC, every date read back shifted by the UTC offset. ## Fix `packages/drizzle-adapter/src/date-columns.ts` holds two helpers, used by both the 0.x and the relations v2 adapters: - `toDriverDate`, called from `customTransformInput`, so it covers create, update, updateMany, `incrementOne` `set`, and where values. When a `Date` is bound for a column whose Drizzle `dataType` is a string type (`"string"` in 0.x, `"string ..."` in 1.x), it writes UTC text: ISO 8601, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm` for MySQL, which is what Drizzle's own MySQL date mode writes. Date-mode columns are untouched. - `fromDriverDate`, called from `customTransformOutput`, reads a date-time without an offset as UTC, as Drizzle's date mode does, and otherwise behaves like `new Date(value)`. The relations v2 adapter had no output transform, so string columns came back as strings there. Detection is per column, so a schema that mixes `text()` and `integer({ mode: "timestamp_ms" })` dates works without a new option. Setting `supportsDates: false` would not work either: it makes the factory send strings to date-mode columns as well, and those call `toISOString()` on whatever they receive. ## Compatibility Schemas generated by the CLI use date-mode columns and see no change. One setup changes behavior: node-postgres or mysql2 with a string column that has no time zone, on a server whose time zone is not UTC. Those drivers accepted a `Date` and wrote it in local time, so existing rows now read back shifted by the server's offset. The changeset says so. ## Tests The e2e tests call the adapter directly on one `user` table and run in `America/Los_Angeles`, so reading a value without a time zone is checked off UTC. - `e2e/adapter/test/drizzle-adapter/adapter.drizzle.string-dates.test.ts` writes, filters on, updates and reads back a `Date` on PostgreSQL via postgres-js (`timestamp({ mode: "string" })`) and SQLite via better-sqlite3 (`text()`). It also checks the stored text. Both tests fail on `main`. With only the write fix, the PostgreSQL test still fails. - `e2e/adapter/test/drizzle-v2-relations-adapter/adapter.drizzle.string-dates.test.ts` does the same for SQLite `text()` on Drizzle 1.0 rc.3, plus a stored value without a time zone. It fails on `main`, and the time-zone case fails with only the write fix. - `packages/drizzle-adapter/src/date-columns.test.ts` covers what the e2e tests can't reach: Drizzle 1.x data type names, the MySQL format, `Date` lists for `in`/`not_in`, offsets, microseconds, and date-only strings. - MySQL `datetime({ mode: "string" })` with mysql2 passed an earlier sign-up version of the e2e test locally. It isn't committed, because the MySQL adapter suite drops and recreates the shared `better_auth` database while other files run. - The full Drizzle 0.45 (1387 tests) and relations v2 (1419 tests) e2e suites pass. `postgres` (already in the lockfile through `e2e/integration/vanilla-node`) is added to the e2e adapter workspace for the postgres-js case. Closes #7419 Closes #10816 Closes #9498 replaced: the write coercion here also covers where values, `incrementOne`, relations v2, Drizzle 1.x data types and UTC reads; thanks @ping-maxwell, credited as co-author Closes #10898 replaced: per-column detection handles mixed `text()` and integer date columns without a new `supportsDates` option --- ## Summary by cubic Drizzle adapters now write dates in string-backed columns as UTC text and read timezone-free values as UTC, preventing driver errors and timezone shifts on writes, where clauses, and `in` / `not_in` filters, plus reads on the relations v2 adapter. **Compatibility** - Existing rows written in server-local time with node-postgres or mysql2 may read back shifted by the server's UTC offset; CLI-generated date columns are unaffected. **Tests** - E2e tests run in `America/Los_Angeles` against PostgreSQL via postgres-js and SQLite via better-sqlite3, covering `timestamp({ mode: "string" })` and `text()` writes, filters, updates, and reads; the relations v2 suite also verifies reading a timezone-free value as UTC. - The unit test covers Drizzle 1.x data types, the MySQL format, Date lists in `in` / `not_in`, explicit offsets, microseconds, and date-only strings. Written for commit 353270cd047d30d3a89ffcaf572f834de97d43ff. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(oauth-provider): make allowedScopes storable across adapters
items.body:
## What
Stores OAuth `allowedScopes` as an empty array `[]` (instead of SQL `NULL`) across all database adapters when omitted, passed as `null`, or passed as `[]`. In `oauthProvider()`, `[]` represents "allow all requested scopes", aligning adapter storage with runtime scope enforcement and fixing issues where database adapters (notably Prisma) coerced `null` or empty fields inconsistently.

Also addresses review-bot feedback:
- **Round-Trip & Schema Compatibility**: Admin create and update schemas now accept `[]`, `null`, or omitted `allowedScopes` as representing an unrestricted resource, restoring full round-trip capability when reading a resource (`GET`) and sending it back (`PATCH`).
- **Whitespace Normalization**: Automatically trims scope entries across both admin endpoints and code-configured seed inputs so exact scope matching (`resolveResourcePolicy`) never fails due to trailing or leading whitespace, while rejecting empty/whitespace-only scope strings.
- **PATCH Safety**: Safely ignores `undefined` in PATCH updates so scope restrictions are never inadvertently cleared. Explicit `null` or `[]` safely transitions allowed scopes to allow-all (`[]`).
- **Docs Clarity**: Updates migration warning in `oauth-provider.mdx` regarding `resourceSeedMode` (defaults to `insertOnly`) and clarifies default MCP resource scope behaviors in `mcp.mdx`.
- **E2E Coverage**: Adds live round-trip tests exercising `adminCreateOAuthResource` and `adminUpdateOAuthResource` on the real adapter.

## Why
Fixes #11725. Previously, storing `allowedScopes` as SQL `NULL` caused adapter deserialization drift—specifically in Prisma, where nullable array columns or relations read back `null` as `[]`, causing the runtime validator to treat resources as restricting all scopes rather than allowing all. By normalizing stored representation to `[]` and accepting both `[]` and `null` as unrestricted in admin schemas, resources behave deterministically across SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB without breaking round-tripping.

## Linked Issue
Fixes #11725

## Breaking Changes
Unrestricted resources now return `allowedScopes: []` instead of `null` on create responses and when read from new/updated rows. Existing database rows with SQL `NULL` continue to return `null` and evaluate as unrestricted until updated. Admin CRUD endpoints now accept `[]`, `null`, and omitted as unrestricted.

## Testing Performed
- Unit & integration tests in `packages/oauth-provider`: 1,184 passed across 44 test suites.
- End-to-end admin endpoint tests in `e2e/adapter/test/adapter-factory/oauth-resource-scope-test-suite.ts` verifying `adminCreateOAuthResource` (omitted scopes -> `[]`), `adminUpdateOAuthResource` (custom scopes -> persisted), and `adminUpdateOAuthResource` (`null` or `[]` -> `[]`).
- TypeScript typecheck (`pnpm exec tsc --noEmit`) clean across all packages.
- Code style & formatting: `biome check` clean across all touched files.

## Risk Tier
Low-to-Medium (Touches OAuth Provider scope storage normalization and admin resource endpoints).

## Rollback Plan
`git revert` the PR commit.

## Reviewer Notes
- The PR is cleanly rebased onto upstream `next`. The historical Cubic bot comment noting "76 files" was from a stale initial commit based on `main` that has since been superseded. The PR touches exactly 13 files in scope.
- Admin PATCH endpoints explicitly differentiate between `undefined` (no-op, preserves existing restrictions) and `null` / `[]` (resets to allow-all).

items.title: Export the schema/DDL renderer so non-kysely adapters can reuse it instead of mirroring getType

labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

items.body:
### Summary

There is no supported way to obtain better-auth's schema DDL for a dialect without also handing it a kysely database. That forces anyone writing a non-kysely adapter to hand-mirror the column rendering, which is easy to get subtly wrong.

`@better-auth/core/db/internal` already exports most of what's needed, and it's genuinely good: `getAuthTablesWithResolvedIndexes` gives the resolved tables, and `getDatabaseFieldIndexName` / `getDatabaseIndexName` give the index naming. Thank you for those — they meant I did not have to mirror plugin table merging, `fieldName` resolution, or index naming.

What is missing is the last mile: the dialect type map and the column renderer. `getType` is a closure **inside** `getMigrations` (`dist/db/get-migration.mjs:436` in 1.7.0-rc.2), as is the `NOT NULL` / `DEFAULT` rendering and the per-field index emission. Nothing in the exports surfaces them, and `getMigrations` itself hard-refuses to help:

```
Only kysely adapter is supported for migrations. You can use `generate` command to generate the schema, if you're using a different adapter.
```
(`dist/db/get-migration.mjs:319`)

So a custom adapter has two options: mirror the renderer, or shell out to the `generate` CLI. Both are worse than a function call.

### Why this comes up

I'm running better-auth inside a Cloudflare **Durable Object**, on the object's own SQLite. That is the only way to get `@better-auth/scim` working on Cloudflare — SCIM requires native transactions, D1 has none, and a DO's `state.storage.transaction()` is a real transaction. But DO storage is not a kysely dialect (and I don't want kysely on the request path), so `getMigrations` is unavailable and the object has to create its own tables.

### Why mirroring is a trap

I mirrored it, carefully, from your source. Then I wrote a test that compiles your DDL via `getMigrations().compileMigrations()` against a throwaway in-memory SQLite and diffs the resulting schema against mine. It found two divergences immediately:

1. **`id` nullability.** You emit `"id" text not null primary key`. I emitted `"id" text primary key` — and in SQLite a `TEXT PRIMARY KEY` still accepts NULL (only `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, the rowid alias, implies NOT NULL). So every one of my tables accepted a NULL id.
2. **Spurious defaults.** I emitted `DEFAULT` for required primitives with a static `defaultValue`, reasoning that a required column might otherwise fail its NOT NULL. Your fresh-table DDL emits none, because you write every field on insert.

Neither was visible without diffing against your output. A third divergence would arrive silently with any release that changes an affinity or adds a constraint kind.

### Proposed API

A pure function that renders the schema for a dialect, with no database argument:

```ts
import { compileSchema } from "@better-auth/core/db";

const statements: string[] = compileSchema(options, { dialect: "sqlite" });
```

Returning statements (or one string) for a create-from-scratch schema would cover the adapter-author case entirely. If that is too large a surface, exporting just the type map would already remove most of the risk:

```ts
import { getColumnType } from "@better-auth/core/db/internal";

getColumnType(field, fieldName, "sqlite"); // → "text" | "integer" | "date" | …
```

Either shape lets a custom adapter reuse your rendering instead of racing it. I'd be happy to open a PR for whichever you prefer — the refactor is mostly lifting `getType` and the column-clause construction out of the `getMigrations` closure, which should be behaviour-preserving for the kysely path.

### Related

- #10551 — `getDatabaseIndexes()` breaking migrations on Cloudflare D1. Same underlying theme: the migration path assumes a kysely-shaped database that Cloudflare's storage primitives don't provide.

Version: `better-auth@1.7.0-rc.2`, `@better-auth/core@1.7.0-rc.2`.

items.title: fix(session): do not restore a revoked session from a stale cache

labels.name: database
labels.description: Database layer, all adapters, schema, migrations

labels.name: devtools

items.body: Closes #11585 Session refresh wrote the cached session before it updated the database. With an eventually consistent cache, that write put a revoked session back for the full session lifetime. The next request accepted it. When a session is stored in the database as well as the cache: - Refresh updates the database first, and only while the row is still live. - The row returned by that write is mirrored to the cache before the `update.after` hooks run. Nothing is read back, so a lagging read replica cannot sign out a new session. - If no live row matches, the cached key and its active session list entry are removed. A before hook that rejects the update leaves the cache as is. - Sign-out deletes the cached key again after the row is deleted or ended. A refresh that runs during the session delete hooks cannot restore it. - A profile update loads the user's session rows with one query, then checks each cached key right before it writes. It always writes the database row. When the cached expiry is later, it rereads the row, so a refresh during the sweep keeps its longer expiry and a shortened session stays short. A lagging replica that still returns a revoked row finds the key already deleted by sign-out. Ended rows are removed. Missing rows are skipped and keep their list entry, because a replica may not have a new row yet. - A profile update raises a list entry to the written expiry, so user-wide revocation can still find the cached session. - Writes with a TTL of 0 are skipped, because some stores treat 0 as no expiry. Sessions stored only in the cache keep the base behavior: each cached copy is read and written back in one step. Writes with a TTL of 0 are skipped. This PR also fixes the Drizzle adapter on MySQL. After an update, it rereads the row with the new values swapped into the `where` clause. A range guard such as `expiresAt > now` became `expiresAt > newExpiresAt` and missed the row, so every refresh returned null. It now swaps in values for equality matches only. ## Known Limits `SecondaryStorage` has no compare-and-set, so two windows remain: - A revocation that lands between the refresh's database write and its cache write can still recreate the key. - The active session list is a read-modify-write, like every other writer of that list. ## Testing - Stale cache reproduction: after refresh, the cache does not hold the revoked session, and the following read returns no session. - A refresh mirrors the updated row to the cache and list. - A refresh on a missing row removes the cached key and list entry. - An update hook that rejects the write leaves the cache in place. - An ended preserved session is not extended. - An update hook that revokes the session does not get it restored. - A refresh that runs while the session is being revoked does not restore it. - A profile update keeps a session created during the sweep. - A profile update does not restore a session signed out while it reads the rows. - A profile update keeps a refresh that lands while it reads the rows. - A profile update does not extend a shortened session from a stale cached copy. - A profile update writes the database expiry to the cache and list. - A profile update does not recreate a deleted session. - A profile update skips the write for a session with less than 1 second left. - Drizzle MySQL rereads keep range guards and swap in new values for equality matches. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes session refresh and profile updates restoring a revoked session from a stale secondary storage cache. Session refresh updates the database first and mirrors the returned row to the cache before `update.after` hooks run. A missing or ended row removes the cached key and its active-sessions entry. Profile updates now read the database rows first, then check each cached key right before writing, so a lagging read replica that still returns a revoked row cannot restore it; without a database they read and write each cached copy in one step. When a cached expiry is later than the row, the sweep rereads the row, so a refresh that lands after the row read is kept and a shortened session is not extended. Sign-out deletes cached keys again after the database rows are removed. - List entries are kept as long as their cached keys so user-wide revocation can still find sessions, and writes with a TTL of 0 are skipped. - Drizzle on MySQL, in both the main adapter and the `relations-v2` entry, now swaps updated values into the `where` clause for equality matches only, so a range guard like `expiresAt > now` still matches the updated row. The adapter suite now checks this too. **Known Limits** `SecondaryStorage` has no compare-and-set, so a revocation that lands between a refresh's database write and its cache write can still recreate the key, and the active-session list is a read-modify-write like every other writer of that list. Written for commit da8aed78dc2d9b6ee681fc42fd2339c311839d04. Summary will update on new commits.

items.body: Fixes #11218. When a session was missing from secondaryStorage (TTL expiry, eviction, flush) but still valid in the database, findSession's database fallback returned it without writing it back - so every subsequent request for that session kept hitting the primary database until the next login. The fallback now repopulates secondaryStorage with the remaining TTL (same shape as createSession's mirror). It also restores the token in the active-sessions index: deleteUserSessions sweeps cached sessions through that index, so a write-back without it would have let a repopulated session survive revoke-all until cache expiry. The existing preserveSessionInDatabase early return is untouched, so revoked-and-preserved rows still can't be restored. Tests: two cases in secondary-storage.test.ts - cache/index repair after a simulated flush, and revoke-all still sweeping a repopulated session. Both fail on main; the full file plus internal-adapter and session-api suites pass with the fix. > Built by breken, your AI support engineer - breken.ai - this one's on us. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #11218. When a session is missing from secondary storage (TTL expiry, eviction, flush) but still valid in the database, `findSession` now writes it back with its remaining TTL and restores the active-sessions index entry, so repeat reads no longer hit the primary DB and revoke-all still sweeps the session. - Cache reads and repair writes are best-effort when a database fallback exists: an outage is logged and treated as a cache miss, and repair failure serves the authoritative database session instead of failing the request. - Without `storeSessionInDatabase`, a secondary-storage outage surfaces as a request error instead of being treated as an invalid session that could clear valid cookies. - Known limitation: a concurrent revoke can race the write-back and leave the token accepted until its session TTL expires; fully closing that needs atomic cache+database coordination. - `preserveSessionInDatabase` early return is unchanged, so revoked-and-preserved rows cannot be resurrected. Summary will update on new commits. --- **Follow-up (review feedback, 2026-09-09):** - The database-fallback cache repair is now **best-effort**: the entire repair block is try/wrapped, so a secondary-storage failure (eviction + unreachable Redis) cannot reject out of `findSession` after the database has already returned the authoritative session - it logs the error and serves the DB result. Matching test: a throwing secondary storage cannot turn `/get-session` into a 500. - **Known limitation (disclosed):** the repair has a residual check-then-act window against a *concurrent* revoke (revocation deletes the database row in flight while this repair repopulates the cache, in which case the token can remain accepted until its session TTL expires). Fully closing this requires atomic cache+database coordination (e.g. a Lua-scripted revoke on Redis, or versioned tokens) - deliberately not shipped as a re-read half-guard that narrows but does not close the race. items.body: The Drizzle adapter's factory config sets `supportsUUIDs`, `supportsJSON` and `supportsArrays` but never `supportsDates`, so the core factory falls back to `true` and `DrizzleAdapterConfig` has no field to change it. That is right for the schema the CLI generates and wrong for date columns declared as `text()`, one of Drizzle's two documented ways to store a SQLite timestamp. `text()` applies no conversion, so the raw `Date` reaches the driver and Cloudflare D1 rejects it with `D1_TYPE_ERROR: Type 'object' not supported`. The `verification` insert is the first write in most flows, so sign-up, social sign-in and session refresh all fail, as do `WHERE expires_at < ?` comparisons. Deriving the flag from `config.provider` would break more than it fixes. Checking `drizzle-orm` source rather than assuming: | Column | Behavior with a `Date` | | --- | --- | | `timestamp()` on PostgreSQL / MySQL | `mapToDriverValue` calls `value.toISOString()` | | `integer({ mode: "timestamp_ms" })` on SQLite | `mapToDriverValue` calls `value.getTime()` | | `text()` on SQLite | no conversion, the `Date` reaches the driver | The CLI generates the first two, and both would throw on a string, so `supportsDates: false` for SQLite (what the Kysely adapter does) would break the schema Better Auth itself generates. Deriving from the column type is wrong too: `supportsDates` is one boolean per adapter, and a schema can mix `text()` and `integer({ mode: "timestamp_ms" })` date columns; expressing that needs a per-column contract. That leaves the escape hatch: `config.supportsDates ?? true`, exposed on `DrizzleAdapterConfig`, added to both the main and `relations-v2` adapters since they carry separate config blocks. Behavior is unchanged for anyone who does not set it. Six cases under a `supportsDates` describe block in `packages/drizzle-adapter/src/drizzle-adapter.test.ts`, on real `sqliteTable` definitions for both schemas, plus two in `relations-v2/drizzle-adapter.test.ts`. Three fail on `main` without the source change; the rest pin the existing default so a later change cannot flip it silently. `pnpm -F @better-auth/drizzle-adapter typecheck` passes, package suite green at 47. I did not run the Docker-backed adapter suites or the e2e tests. Fixes #10816 ## AI disclosure This was written with AI assistance. Per the AI policy in CONTRIBUTING.md, I have reviewed the change, verified the Drizzle column behavior in `drizzle-orm` source rather than assuming it, and can discuss the reasoning above. --- ## Summary by cubic Add a `supportsDates` option to the Drizzle adapters in `@better-auth/drizzle-adapter`, defaulting to true. Previously the adapter always passed `Date` objects through; apps using SQLite `text()` date columns couldn’t change this and hit Cloudflare D1 type errors. Now you can disable passthrough so Better Auth serializes to ISO strings on writes and where operands, and parses on reads. - Migration: If your SQLite schema stores timestamps as `text()`, set `supportsDates: false` in the Drizzle adapter config to avoid driver rejections. - Caution: Do not set `supportsDates: false` when using Drizzle `timestamp` columns (PostgreSQL/MySQL) or SQLite `integer({ mode: "timestamp_ms" })`; those expect a `Date` and will fail. Written for commit b375e39a4d2c0e62eab3d59c357f85cdba297745. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: fix(organization): apply beforeAddTeamMember data and allow teamMember additionalFields

labels.name: organization
labels.description: Org, teams, roles, permissions, admin, access control

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Documentation, demos

items.body: Fixes #10707. ## What `beforeAddTeamMember` is typed `Promise }>`, the same as `beforeCreateTeam` and `beforeUpdateTeam`. It does not honour that return value. At `routes/crud-team.ts` the call site read the hook's result, tested it, and then did nothing with it: ```ts if (response && typeof response === "object" && "data" in response) { // Allow the hook to modify the data } ``` The plugin has ten `"data" in response` sites and this was the only one with an empty body. `git log -L` puts its origin in bba0a42ee ("feat(organization): organization life cycle hooks"), the same PR that added the working siblings — so it shipped empty rather than having been broken later. The comment describes the opposite of what the block does. Fixing that alone is not enough to make the reporter's case work. `teamMember` was also the only one of the plugin's six org-owned models whose schema option omitted `additionalFields` — the other five all carry it. Since `transformInput` iterates the *declared* fields (`packages/core/src/db/adapter/factory.ts:210`) and never `Object.keys(data)`, an undeclared key is dropped silently before it reaches any adapter. So the hook had nothing it could legally write, and the two defects are only observable together. That gap looks like scope drift rather than a decision: `additionalFields` landed in 93698afd4, whose title names exactly the four models that existed then; `teamMember` arrived later with only `modelName` + `fields`, and the next model added after it (`organizationRole`) did ship with `additionalFields`. ## How - `types.ts` / `organization.ts` — give `teamMember` the `additionalFields` option and spread it into the model's fields, matching the five siblings. - `routes/crud-team.ts` — capture `response.data` and pass it to both insert paths. There are two: `addTeamMemberWithLimit` when `teams.maximumMembersPerTeam` is set, and `findOrCreateTeamMember` otherwise. Threading only the second would have left the seat-limited path silently dropping hook data, so both are covered and both are tested. - `adapter.ts` — thread the fields through to `createTeamMemberWithKey`, the single `adapter.create({ model: "teamMember" })` in non-test source. They are spread **first**, so `teamId` / `userId` / `membershipKey` / `createdAt` are re-applied after and stay authoritative. That ordering is load-bearing, not tidiness: - the route validates the team, the target user's org membership and the user record *before* the hook runs, so a merged `{ data: { teamId: "…" } }` would insert into a team that was never checked; - `membershipKey` is declared `input: false`, but nothing in `packages/core/src/db/adapter/` enforces `input: false` — `transformInput` has no such check. The ordering is the only thing protecting the unique membership key. - `adapter.ts` — `stripTeamMembershipKey` now runs through `filterOutputFields`. Every teamMember-returning path used that hand-rolled helper instead of `filterOutputFields`, which is what enforces `returned: false` for the siblings; enabling `additionalFields` without this would have leaked any field declared `returned: false`. - `client.ts` — `OrganizationClientOptions["schema"]` listed five models and omitted `teamMember` too. Without this, declaring `teamMember` fields on the client fails to compile, and the documented `inferOrgAdditionalFields` pattern fails with `TS2559: has no properties in common` when `teamMember` is the only model with additional fields — which is exactly the reported use case. `computeTeamMembershipKey` still hashes only `[teamId, userId]`, so no additional field can perturb the dedup key or the unique index. Nothing under `packages/core` is touched. ## Direction — worth a maintainer's call I implemented the reading that the type signature promises. The honest counter-argument is that this hook's JSDoc never advertised the mutation: "You can return a `data` object to override the default data." appears seven times in `types.ts` and never for `beforeAddTeamMember`, and the docs example only validates and throws. The alternative is narrowing the return type to `Promise` and admitting the hook is validate-only. I did not take it because the TypeScript contract is unambiguous and identical to two hooks that *do* honour it, and because narrowing is a breaking type change for anyone returning data today — currently a silent no-op, afterwards a compile error — with no runtime benefit. If you would rather have the narrowing, say so and I will swap it; the failing test is already here either way. Two smaller semantics I picked and would happily change: - **Re-add applies nothing.** Both adapter methods are find-or-create, so when the membership already exists the existing row is returned untouched. I think not silently rewriting an established membership is right, but it does differ from `beforeUpdateTeam`. - **`createdAt` stays authoritative**, unlike `beforeCreateTeam`, which lets the hook override it. One rule seemed easier to explain than two: the hook adds fields, it does not rewrite the row's identity or timestamp. ## Scope Section 3 of the issue — that only the dedicated endpoint fires teamMember hooks — is deliberately **not** here. The other three insert paths (`crud-org.ts`, `crud-members.ts`, `crud-invites.ts`) create rows without running this hook, so hook-supplied fields are absent there. Changing that changes *when hooks fire*, which is an API decision rather than a bug fix. It is now stated in the docs example so nobody adopts the pattern expecting full coverage, and I am glad to follow up if you want it. ## Verification Baseline captured on `main` @ 64da15b0b before any edit; `pnpm test` avoided per AGENTS.md, so this is the organization plugin suite. | | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | `vitest run src/plugins/organization/` | 253 passed, 1 todo | **257 passed, 1 todo** | | `pnpm typecheck` | exit 2 | **exit 0** | | `biome check` (26 files) | clean | clean | Zero pre-existing failures, and no test that passed in the baseline fails now. All four new tests were watched failing before the fix: - `should declare teamMember additional fields on the table` — the schema spread, via `getAuthTables` - `should apply data returned from beforeAddTeamMember` — end to end on the find-or-create path, including `returned: false` filtering - `applies the hook data on the seat-limited insert path` — the `maximumMembersPerTeam` path the report never reaches - `lets the client schema declare teamMember additional fields` — the client-side gap The compile-time half of the bug reproduces as `TS2353` on the `satisfies` form and `TS2769` on the `organization({ … })` call form. Changeset included (`better-auth: patch`). Parts of this were written with AI assistance; I have reviewed the change and can discuss any of it. --- ## Summary by cubic Applies `beforeAddTeamMember` returned data and adds `schema.teamMember.additionalFields`, so member-level fields persist and round-trip like other org models. Previously the hook’s data was ignored and undeclared fields were dropped. - Threads `additionalFields` from the route through the adapter into both insert paths (find-or-create and seat-limited). `teamId`, `userId`, `membershipKey`, and `createdAt` remain authoritative and override hook data. - Filters `teamMember` responses via `filterOutputFields` to honor `returned: false`; `membershipKey` remains server-only. - Extends server types and client `OrganizationClientOptions["schema"]` to include `teamMember.additionalFields`, unblocking `inferOrgAdditionalFields`. - Docs clarify limits (hook runs only on `addTeamMember`, applies on insert only), require optional or `defaultValue` fields for other creation paths, and the example now declares the `teamMember` field it returns. **Migration** - Declare `schema.teamMember.additionalFields` on both server and client if you want to store extra member-level data. - Make those fields optional or give them a `defaultValue` if you also add members via `createOrganization`, `addMember`, or `acceptInvitation` (these do not invoke the hook). - Do not rely on overriding `teamId`, `userId`, `membershipKey`, or `createdAt` in the hook; they are ignored. Written for commit 50f9c940c4e3a3c0a3864d8d688bf1f0a1503255. Summary will update on new commits.

items.title: feat(ciba): add backchannel authentication plugin

labels.name: identity
labels.description: OAuth/OIDC provider, device flow

items.body:
## Summary

Adds `@better-auth/ciba`, OpenID Connect Client-Initiated Backchannel Authentication for `oauthProvider()`, for clients such as agents and CLIs that cannot drive a browser the user trusts. It supports poll and ping delivery, `login_hint`, DPoP, RFC 8707 resources, and RFC 9396 `authorization_details`. It reuses what the device grant and the provider already have:

```text
POST /oauth2/bc-authorize          createOAuthEndpoint: CIBA §13 errors, form only (§7.1), repeated params rejected
  provider.authenticateClient      credentials required (§7.1) unless allowPublicClients
  client metadata                  backchannel_token_delivery_mode, backchannel_client_notification_endpoint (§4),
                                   validated at registration through the clientMetadata extension (#11767)
  resolveResourcePolicy            same check as the device grant
  validateRequest hook             reject by policy (acr_values, RAR), set additionalFields
GET  /ciba/requests | /ciba/request   owner session; by request_id or auth_req_id
POST /ciba/approve | /ciba/deny       owner session      ┐ one guarded transition (incrementOne),
auth.api.completeCibaRequest          server-only        ┘ then ping like back-channel logout
POST /oauth2/token (CIBA grant)
  redeemPolledAuthorization        poll, slow_down, expiry, denial, atomic single-use claim
  beforeTokenIssuance hook         full row; refuse (row stays approved) or add claims
  provider.issueTokens             auth_time from the approving session, DPoP via confirmation
```

`redeemPolledAuthorization` is the device grant's `redeemDeviceCode` state machine, generalized over model and lookup; `redeemDeviceCode` now wraps it unchanged. The oauth-provider helpers CIBA calls are exported from the first-party `@better-auth/oauth-provider/internal` entry.

A ping-mode request keeps its `auth_req_id` encrypted with the server secret so a completion by `request_id` can still send the ping (§10.2 requires the raw value in the callback).

Left out:
- Push delivery: its ID token needs `rt_hash` (§10.3.1), which the provider can't add yet.
- Achieved `acr`/`amr` in ID tokens: the provider still reports `acr: "0"`. `acr_values` are stored and passed to the hooks.
- `id_token_hint` and `login_hint_token`: rejected explicitly.
- Changing `authorization_details` at approval.

## Evidence

- **Before:** after merging `next`, every test fails in setup (the fixture's redirect URI is now rejected), and a form-encoded `bc-authorize` request returns 500 `TypeError: unusable`.
  **After:** `packages/ciba` has 57 passing tests, all form-encoded, covering both delivery modes, approval by either identifier, server completion with ping, both hooks, `additionalFields`, RAR, public clients, DPoP, and repeated `resource` values. The device grant's own suites pass unchanged. Typecheck passes for better-auth, oauth-provider and ciba.
- **Black box:** `e2e/integration/vanilla-node/e2e/ciba.spec.ts` runs the provider, the client's HTTPS notification receiver, and the approving user (a browser context) as separate parties over real sockets. It covers approval from the pending list, cross-client isolation, single-use issuance, ping on a browser denial and on server completion by `request_id`, no redirect following from the client endpoint, and refusal of a non-https endpoint. With ping delivery disabled, both ping scenarios fail.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

New, unreleased package. The `cibaRequest` table is created only for deployments that add `ciba()`.

**Blast Radius:** device-authorization

`redeemDeviceCode` now delegates to the shared function. Its signature, error codes, and messages are unchanged, and its suites pass.

items.title: fix(oauth-provider): stop writing configured resources during init
items.body:
### What
Fixes #11725 (Part 2) by eliminating all database I/O and row writes during `betterAuth()` construction with configured `resources` or `mcp({ resource })`.

### Why
Previously, constructing `betterAuth()` with configured resources eagerly called `seedResourcesOnce` during plugin initialization. This caused:
- Eager database operations (`oauthResource.findOne` + `create`) during module import/startup.
- Blocked context resolution during `next build`, `auth generate`, and unit tests that never use OAuth.
- Writes to production databases with build/CLI credentials.
- Reliance on error-string matching (`MISSING_TABLE_PATTERN`) and post-insert re-reads to survive unmigrated databases or concurrent boots.
- A second lazy seed call inside `getResource` on the first token/authorization read.

### Implementation Details
1. **Zero-I/O In-Memory Indexing**: Configured resources are normalized and indexed synchronously in memory (`indexConfiguredResources`) into a per-options `WeakMap` during plugin creation with zero database queries.
2. **Read-Time Resource Combine**:
   - `combineResource` synchronously combines persisted database rows with in-memory configured entries per `resourceSeedMode`:
     - `insertOnly` (default): database row wins once it exists; configured entry used if no row.
     - `merge`: present configured fields override row values; omitted fields preserve row values.
     - `overwrite`: configured values replace row values while preserving persistent row identity (`id`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `policyVersion`).
   - `getResource` reads only stored rows and combines config post-lookup.
   - `getResourceCustomClaims` resolves config-only entries alongside stored rows using a single `findMany` query.
   - Admin `listResourcesEndpoint` concatenates stored rows with unpersisted configured entries (`getConfiguredResourcesWithoutRows`).
3. **Lazy, Idempotent Row Creation**:
   - Implemented `ensureResourceRow` with an in-process single-flight lock (`withResourceInsertLock`) and unique-constraint race recovery (re-reading the winner row if a concurrent process inserts first).
   - Rows are created only when an external foreign key needs one (before writing `oauthClientResource` links during client registration or admin link endpoints) or when an admin updates a row-less configured resource.
4. **Complete Seed Machinery Removal**:
   - Removed init seed hook, `seedResources`, `seedResourcesOnce`, `SeedState`, `seedStates`, `getSeedState`, `resetSeedStateForTests`, `logStartupSeedFailure`, `buildSeedUpdate`, `MISSING_TABLE_PATTERN`, and the lazy seed inside `getResource`.
   - Removed all Part 2 markers (`TODO(#11725)`) while preserving all Part 1 markers (`FIXME(#11725)`) intact.
5. **Documentation & Changeset**:
   - Updated `oauth-provider.mdx` and `mcp.mdx` to reflect in-memory configuration and lazy row creation.
   - Added minor changeset `.changeset/lazy-oauth-resource-rows.md` targeting `@better-auth/oauth-provider`.

### Verification
- 8 hermetic test suites passed (291/291 tests green):
  - Zero-I/O construction verified (`resource-startup.test.ts`: 0 adapter calls and 0 rows created).
  - Config-only token issuance, policy enforcement, and custom claims introspection verified.
  - Concurrent dynamic client registration single-row creation verified (`register.test.ts`).
  - Read-time mode matrix (`insertOnly`, `merge`, `overwrite`) verified (`resources.test.ts`).
  - Admin CRUD on row-less configured resources verified (`oauthResource/endpoints.test.ts`).
  - Memoized deferred identifier validation on read verified.
- `pnpm --filter @better-auth/oauth-provider typecheck`: Clean (Exit 0).
- `pnpm biome check`: Clean (Exit 0).
- Build output (`tsdown`): Clean (Exit 0).
- Exact 1 commit, exactly 17 authorized files, zero core schema/DDL modifications.

items.body:
## Summary
- `POST /one-tap/nonce` issues a short-lived nonce bound to the browser with a signed HttpOnly cookie and a single-use verification record
- `oneTap()` fetches that nonce before Google initializes (prompt and button modes) and ignores caller-provided `nonce` values
- `/one-tap/callback` verifies the ID token's `nonce` claim against the server-issued value, then consumes the attempt so a captured token cannot be replayed
- Button mode refreshes the nonce after each credential callback and shortly before TTL expiry, so a long-lived Sign in with Google button does not keep a consumed or expired nonce
- A browser may hold a small, bounded set of outstanding attempts, so concurrent buttons and a refresh landing between a click and its callback no longer invalidate each other
- A failed nonce refresh retries with backoff instead of stranding the button on a spent nonce

Closes #10926

#### Concurrent attempts

A browser previously held exactly one outstanding nonce state, so any new `/one-tap/nonce` call invalidated a nonce Google may already have minted a credential against — rejecting a legitimate sign-in with a 400 whenever a scheduled refresh landed mid-click or a page rendered more than one button.

The signed cookie now carries a bounded set of outstanding states, and the callback matches the token's verified `nonce` claim against that set, consuming only the record it matched and leaving siblings alive. Replay protection is unchanged: the cookie is signed and HttpOnly so the candidate set is not attacker-controlled, and every record stays single-use.

#### Test plan
- [x] One Tap tests cover matching nonce, mismatched claim, missing cookie, replay, and button-mode refresh
- [x] Added coverage for cross-attempt acceptance, replay of a consumed attempt while a sibling is outstanding, and the client refresh-retry path
- [x] `vitest run src/plugins/one-tap` — 34 passed; the three new tests fail against the pre-fix source
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean for one-tap (also clears two pre-existing `container is possibly null` errors)

items.body:
## Summary

Fixes #11207.

`guardProviderMutation` previously required an adapter with an interactive transaction callback. On Cloudflare D1 (Drizzle) the adapter has no `transaction` function, so `PATCH`/`DELETE /sso/update-provider` and `/sso/delete-provider` were rejected with `501 SSO_PROVIDER_MUTATION_GUARD_REQUIRES_NATIVE_TRANSACTIONS`.

This keeps the existing lock → guard → write transaction path for adapters that support native transactions, and adds an automatic optimistic-concurrency path for adapters that do not:

- The guard evaluates a snapshot of the provider row (including `issuer`, `oidcConfig`, `samlConfig`, `domain`, `domainVerified`, and scalar columns).
- Updates apply as a compare-and-swap against that snapshot using `updateMany`'s affected-row count, which is normalized across Drizzle drivers (including MySQL and D1). A concurrent change affects zero rows and returns `409 SSO_PROVIDER_CHANGED`.
- A zero-row result is accepted only for a true no-op, and only after re-reading the unchanged snapshot. This handles MySQL `changedRows` and MongoDB `modifiedCount` without treating a concurrent save as success.
- After a successful update, the response is read back with predicates on the fields this request wrote, so adapter `onUpdate`/output transforms are returned without accepting another request's value.
- Operations that depend on serializing account linking are refused in optimistic mode rather than silently weakening their guarantees:
  - Identity-boundary changes return `501 SSO_PROVIDER_IDENTITY_CHANGE_REQUIRES_NATIVE_TRANSACTIONS`.
  - Deleting a provider with linked accounts returns `501 SSO_PROVIDER_DELETE_WITH_LINKED_ACCOUNTS_REQUIRES_NATIVE_TRANSACTIONS`. Optimistic mode no longer performs non-atomic account cleanup.
  - Writing a non-scalar additional field returns `501 SSO_PROVIDER_NON_SCALAR_UPDATE_REQUIRES_NATIVE_TRANSACTIONS`, because equality predicates can only fence scalar columns.
- Deletion of a provider without linked accounts is a snapshot CAS on the provider row.
- Guard writes are not rolled back in optimistic mode. Docs describe guards as read-only guidance, and the D1 setup guidance is documented.

No public TypeScript API changes; only JSDoc and docs were updated.

## Tests

- Added regression tests covering optimistic update success, update conflict, no-op success, no-op conflict, guard rejection, identity-change rejection, non-scalar update rejection, adapter-updated response values, delete success, delete conflict, delete-with-linked-accounts rejection, and a real Kysely/node:sqlite adapter with `transaction: false`.
- Replaced the two tests that asserted the `501` refusal.
- Full suite: `132 passed, 4 failed`. The 4 failures are the Postgres tests that require `docker compose up -d` (`ECONNREFUSED 5432`).

```text
pnpm typecheck                             # passed
pnpm biome check (changed TS files)        # passed
pnpm vitest packages/sso/src/providers.test.ts --run
# 132 passed, 4 failed (Postgres ECONNREFUSED)
```

`.changeset/sso-provider-guard-d1.md` — patch for `@better-auth/sso`.

items.body: `reserveVerificationValue` writes a replay marker keyed by a deterministic primary key, a SHA-256 of `reserve:`, so a second caller collides with the first and gets `false`. The digest was base64url encoded, and that string is not a valid UUID. With `advanced.database.generateId: "uuid"` the adapter drops the id and puts a random UUID in its place, so every replay wrote its own row and got `true` back. The SAML assertion replay check in the sso plugin never fired. On adapters that generate UUIDs in the database the insert fails with a NOT NULL error instead. The derivation stays the same. Under the uuid strategy the first 16 bytes of the digest are now formatted as a name based UUID, which passes the check and is still a pure function of the identifier. Other strategies keep the base64url key, so no existing rows change shape. `serial` cannot hold a derived id at all, so it throws instead of reporting a reservation that did not happen. Two tests go in the existing `reserveVerificationValue` block. Both fail before this change. Closes #10624. Written with AI assistance, reviewed and tested by me. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes verification reservations in `better-auth` when `advanced.database.generateId: "uuid"`, restoring SAML assertion replay protection. items.body:
`/revoke-other-sessions` called `deleteSession` once per other session, and each call runs a lookup and a delete, so the endpoint cost two queries per session. It now passes the tokens to `internalAdapter.deleteSessions`, which the multi-session plugin already uses. The query count no longer depends on the number of sessions: revoking 3 or 9 other sessions both take one `findOne`, two `findMany` and one `deleteMany`.

To keep the old per-session behavior, `deleteSessions` changed too:
- `session.delete.before` now runs per row (new `deleteEachWithHooks` helper). A hook that returns `false` keeps only that session, and the rest are still deleted in one statement.
- With secondary storage, the cache key and the `active-sessions-<userId>` entry are removed after the database delete, and only for sessions that were actually deleted, the same way `deleteUserSessions` works since #10687. Before, `deleteSessions` dropped every key up front, so a vetoed session vanished from `listSessions` while staying usable through the database, and revoked tokens stayed in the index until its TTL.
- The hook lookup uses the batch size as its limit, so vetoes past `defaultFindManyLimit` still count. If the lookup fails, the sessions are still deleted without hooks, like `deleteManyWithHooks`, and a failed cache cleanup after commit is logged instead of returning a 500.

The multi-session plugin's sign-out and session-limit cleanup also go through `deleteSessions`, so they get the same behavior. The response is still `{ status: true }` when a hook vetoes a session, same as the old loop and `/revoke-session`.

The tests in `session-api.test.ts` cover a veto on one session, a veto with `storeSessionInDatabase` and `preserveSessionInDatabase` (the vetoed session stays cached and listed), the `active-sessions` list in all three secondary storage modes, and the adapter call count for 3 vs 9 sessions. Three more cover vetoes past `defaultFindManyLimit`, a failed hook lookup, and a failed cache cleanup.

`deleteSession` (single token) still clears the cache before its hook runs. I left it alone to keep this focused.

#10138 touches the same lines for a different bug (the session list is capped at `defaultFindManyLimit`), so whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

Closes #11433

items.body: Refs #10315 ## Summary A request-scoped runtime, such as Cloudflare Workers, stops settling a promise once the request that created it responds. Better Auth cached two such promises for the life of the isolate: initialization and the schema check. When the first request responded before either settled, every later request in the isolate waited on it. This PR bounds and retries both. ```diff betterAuth(options) - context = init(options) + (starts nothing) joinAuthContext() # each request, API call and auth.$context read - return context + if an attempt settled + return it + if the attempt in flight is past its 30s deadline + evict it + attempt ??= init(options), handed to advanced.backgroundTasks.handler + return attempt, or reject at the deadline with a BetterAuthError that names the cause checkSchema(logger) - return the cached lookup + evict a pending lookup past 30s, warn once through the caller's logger, and proceed ``` `better-auth/cloudflare` exports `withCloudflare`. It sets `advanced.backgroundTasks.handler` to `waitUntil`, so the runtime keeps settling initialization and the schema check after the first request responds. Without it, a request that joins dropped initialization waits 30s and fails, and the next request retries. ```ts import { withCloudflare } from "better-auth/cloudflare"; export const auth = betterAuth(withCloudflare({ database: env.DB })); ``` Telemetry reports one install for each auth instance across retries. Reading `auth.$context` at module scope settles. The Workers runtime refuses a timer at global scope, so that read has no 30s bound. No request exists there to drop it. This PR leaves the module-level `import("node:async_hooks")` in `packages/core/src/async_hooks/index.ts` unchanged. #10318 addresses that import. Reports in #10315 of hangs with a fresh `betterAuth()` per request point at it, since a fresh instance holds a fresh context. ## Evidence - **Before:** workerd smoke tests, with the `withCloudflare` handler replaced by one that holds nothing: ```text × settles initialization for a later request after the request that started it responded 5006ms × settles the schema check for a later request after the request that started it responded 5004ms Tests 2 failed | 1 passed (3) ``` **After:** ```text e2e/smoke/test/fixtures/cloudflare Tests 12 passed (12) ``` - Unit tests with fake timers. On `main`, a joiner waits for as long as initialization stays pending. ```text base.test.ts init never settles, a request joins, advance 30s rejects with BetterAuthError the next request joins starts a fresh initialization schema-check.test.ts lookup never settles, a caller joins, advance 30s resolves without a verdict warns once through the caller's logger ``` - Runtime probes under miniflare (wrangler `createTestHarness`, `compatibility_date` 2026-08-17, `nodejs_compat`). The probe code is not part of this PR. | Probe | Result | | --- | --- | | Module-scope `import("node:async_hooks")` | Settled during module evaluation, before the first request | | Client aborts a request after 250ms | A later request saw the import, the ALS storage and a request-scoped timer settle | | Handler responds before its work settles | The import and the ALS storage stayed settled. A timer armed in that request stayed pending | | `waitUntil` at module scope | Threw "Disallowed operation called within global scope". `betterAuth(withCloudflare(...))` at module scope did not throw | - Before the timer fix, the workerd smoke test for a module-scope `auth.$context` read failed with `rejected:Error: Disallowed operation called within global scope. ... setting a timeout ... are not allowed within global scope`. After it, the read settles. - Local: `pnpm typecheck` passes. `packages/better-auth` `src/auth src/context src/api`: 669 passed. `packages/core` `src/db src/utils`: 330 passed. `e2e/smoke` Cloudflare fixture: 12 passed. ## Merge Danger **Door:** two-way A revert restores the previous behaviour. The `better-auth/cloudflare` export becomes one-way once released, because removing it breaks importers. **Blast Radius:** every auth instance - `betterAuth()` no longer starts initialization. Init errors, schema mismatch logs and the telemetry init event appear on the first request or `auth.$context` read. The changeset is `patch`, since neither change needs user action. - Reads of `auth.$context` can return different promises for the same context. - On a runtime that keeps settling promises, such as Node.js, initialization that stalls past 30s leads the next request to start a second attempt while the first runs. Each attempt creates its own adapter and runs each plugin's `init`. The bound stays when a handler is set, because `waitUntil` holds a promise for [at most 30 seconds after the request ends](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/runtime-apis/context/#waituntil), and a handler can return without holding the promise. - `withCloudflare` routes every background task, including `runInBackground`, to `waitUntil`. - An attempt claims the telemetry install report before it awaits telemetry. If that attempt is dropped inside telemetry, or stalls past 30s and then fails after a second attempt skipped the report, the instance reports no install. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes requests hanging on Cloudflare Workers when the runtime drops Better Auth initialization or the schema check after the request that started them responds (Refs #10315). - Better Auth no longer starts initialization at construction; it starts on the first request or `auth.$context` read, is bounded at 30 seconds, and the next request retries a dropped or failed attempt. Function-based contexts are now resolved at every call site, so plugin middleware receives the actual context instead of the thunk. - The schema check is bounded the same way: a caller past the bound proceeds without a verdict, logs a warning, and the next request asks the database again. - New `better-auth/cloudflare` export `withCloudflare` sets `advanced.backgroundTasks.handler` to the runtime's `waitUntil`, keeping initialization, the schema check, and the telemetry install report settling after the starting request responds. - Telemetry defers the install event and sends it once from the attempt that becomes the instance's context, so each auth instance reports exactly one install; the report settles only when the send finishes, so `waitUntil` holds the request until then. **Migration** - `betterAuth()` no longer starts initialization, so init errors, schema mismatch logs, and the telemetry init event appear on first use. - Each `auth.$context` read returns a new promise resolving to the same context. - On runtimes that reject timers outside a request, module-scope reads are unbounded; elsewhere a stalled attempt can run alongside the retry. - The changeset is `patch`; `better-auth/cloudflare` becomes a one-way export once released. Written for commit af5cc1da88323d3a81ad4905d148bd4ab3b3a131. Summary will update on new commits.
